infra-bot: [1760123456] NOTICE: sudden interruption wave in eu-west1-gpu pool, ~18% of preemptible GPUs evicted in last 5m. Affected node labels: gpu-v2-rt, gpu-v2-batch. Services with streaming KV cache show tail latency spikes.
maya: saw the same, long-running streams spiking to 2.4s p95 on grpc endpoints.
jules: confirm - model-serving pods on nodegroup gpu-v2-rt got bounced, KV caches lost so requests hit cold path.
sam: is this an AZ bird? or region-wide preemptible schedule?
aditya: looks regional. GCE preemptible churn graph -> https://metrics/reorg/evictions?region=eu-west1 shows a sharp pulse at 1760123400-1760123500.
maya: quick mitigation idea: shift streaming traffic to dedicated pool in eu-west1-dc (dedicated-1), enable short-circuit fallback that serves trimmed responses to reduce mem pressure. Thoughts?
jules: +1 for fallback route, but need to coordinate rollout. If we blast all streams to dedicated we might hit quota.
oncall-steph: oncall here. I can flip routing policy to prefer dedicated for 10% of streams for 5m, then increase if stable. Doing it in 2m.
kyle: also consider draining stateful pods gracefully instead of immediate eviction fallback — add preStop hook to flush KV to remote cache (redis) next deploy.
aditya: infra note: autoscaler didn't react because pods were pending GPU quota; cluster autoscaler needs a soft-capacity bump for preemption spikes. Suggested temp patch: allow burstup to 12 nodes in pool.
sam: can we change preemptible:mixed_ratio to 60:40 (preemptible:on-demand) for gpu-v2-rt? Cost impact calc?
maya: rough calc: moving 20% to on-demand ~ +$6k/month for eu-west1 traffic, reduces evictions by ~70% per historical windows. Might be worth it for customer-facing streaming.
jules: ok let's do immediate tactical sequence: 1) @oncall-steph switch 10% pref to dedicated and enable fallback; 2) aditya bump burstup cap to 12 nodes; 3) kyle start rolling deploy with preStop KV flush; 4) maya throttle long-lived streams to new short session mode.
oncall-steph: executing step 1 now -> `/infra route-policy set --pool=streaming --prefer=dedicated --weight=10 --duration=5m`
aditya: bumping burst cap -> `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling gpu-v2-rt --max-num-replicas=12` (started)
kyle: kicking rolling deploy with preStop hook; small canary 5%. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving --selector=canary-tier=small`
sam: monitoring logs. initial p95 down from 2.4s to 1.1s for canary after fallback route. good signal.
maya: thanks. also let's add a short PromQL to track eviction pressure: `sum(rate(node_eviction_count{region="eu-west1"}[5m])) by (instance_group)`
aditya: added alert rule for >10% eviction rate across pool for 5m.
jules: medium-term: reduce rate of preemptible-only pools for streaming critical lanes. We should create a cost/availability runway doc to present trade-offs to biz.
maya: will draft doc with numbers and recommended fallback defaults.
oncall-steph: follow-ups: 1) status check in 30m; 2) ticket to infra backlog to implement persistent KV spillover; 3) sales/customer comm if we see continued user-facing errors.
kyle: posting small postmortem template in #postmortems once stabilized.
aditya: metrics look stable now, evictions down to 2% in last 5m, streaming p95 ~380ms.
sam: closing loop here but keeping monitoring on for next 2h. :eyes:
maya: thanks team. filing cost/availability ticket: INFRA-7821.
infra-bot: [1760124620] NOTE: automated runbook executed: route-policy change + autoscaler bump. Logged under incident-id infra-2026-03-eu-gpu-evict.
